title: Thresholded region-skew router with per-tenant budget slices and GPU SKU affinity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers experience unpredictable spend and degraded P99 latency when requests are routed aggressively to spot GPUs or to remote regions without accounting for short-term spend patterns. Current routing policies favor cost or latency heuristics independently; we need a unified policy that enforces per-tenant soft budget slices while still honoring latency SLOs and graceful model-variant degradation.

Goals:
- Implement a routing policy that enforces per-tenant budget slices (daily/hourly) with soft caps and configurable grace windows.
- Use a GPU SKU affinity score to prefer accelerators most cost-effective for the model class and sequence-length profile.
- Hedge against spot eviction risk by distributing concurrent allocations across at least two distinct fault domains (region or instance family) when budget permits.
- Support deterministic fallback to smaller/quantized model variants when spend approaches a hard cap or when throughput would otherwise violate budget constraints.
- Provide telemetry and failure modes that are observable in Console (per-tenant spend burn-down, headroom, evictions, fallback trigger counts).

Design summary:
1) Budget slices: each tenant gets a rolling budget window (configurable, default 1h). The router tracks spend burn-down as token-weighted units using existing cost-estimator. Two thresholds: soft_threshold (e.g., 80%) triggers degraded cost preference and hedging; hard_threshold (e.g., 100%) triggers deterministic fallback policies. Soft threshold is a "hint" that allows graceful degradation rather than abrupt rejection.

2) SKU affinity scoring: we compute a per-tenant, per-model SKU affinity score combining recent latency, throughput, and per-token cost. The score is normalized and used as an additive term in the routing selection function to bias selection toward GPU SKUs that hit performance targets at lower unit cost. Affinity is updated asynchronously on a minute cadence.

3) Hedging and regional skew: when soft_threshold is exceeded, router switches from a single-preference region to a skewed fan-out that allocates new requests across at least two regions / instance families to reduce correlated spot eviction risk. Allocation fractioning is proportional to SKU affinity and ephemeral headroom.

4) Model variant fallbacks: define a fallback graph per model family with mappings: full->quantized-8->small-variant. Fallback triggers: hard_threshold breach or sustained (>30s) inability to place requests within latency headroom. Fallback actions include: reduce token budget (truncate long completions), switch model variant, or reject non-critical low-priority requests.

5) Config/API: add new routing policy schema to tenant config: {budget_window, soft_threshold, hard_threshold, hedging_enabled, min_regions, sku_affinity_weights, fallback_graph, priority_rules}. Implement admin API for policy previews and dry-run mode.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Spend burn-down (tokens and $) per tenant per budget window.
- Headroom gauge: amount of budget left in current slice.
- Fallback trigger log with reasons.
- Hedging effectiveness: eviction rate delta pre/post-hedge.

Operational constraints and risk mitigations:
- We will default hedging to disabled for tenants on small free tiers to avoid cross-region bandwidth charges.
- Rollout will start as dry-run for 2 weeks using simulated enforcement (Console flags) to collect metrics.
- Security review required for admin API changes (exposes budget manipulation endpoints).

Acceptance criteria:
- Router enforces soft_threshold behavior and switches to hedged routing in >95% of simulated soft-threshold scenarios.
- Hard_threshold results in deterministic fallback mapping applied within 500ms of detection for 99% of cases.
- End-to-end P50 latency degradation under soft_threshold remains <15% vs baseline for 95% of requests.
- Per-tenant spend telemetry appears in Console and correlates with billing within 3% over 24h.
- Integration tests for evictions: simulating spot preemptions yields lower end-user impact with hedging enabled (measured by completion ratio).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/thresholded-region-skew-router
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287
- Cost estimator util: https://github.com/redwood-inference/common/tree/main/cost-estimator

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated dry-run for 2 weeks (collect metrics).
2) Canary enforcement for 5 tenants (manual enable).
3) Gradual ramp: enable on 25% of production traffic with auto-rollback on metric regressions.
4) Full rollout after 6 weeks of stable telemetry.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Triage: flagged as high ROI for mid-market customers with tight monthly budgets. PM suggests adding a per-route priority override.
2026-03-02 - Design review with SRE and Runtime: agreed on async SKU affinity updates to avoid hotpath serialization. SRE requested hedging minimum of 2 fault domains.

2026-03-05 - Prototype run: simulated tenant with 1h window, soft_threshold=75% showed 42% reduction in sudden spend spikes during batch retries, median latency +8%. Added additional metrics to track per-model fallback rate.
2026-03-09 - Security: initial assessment indicates admin API needs audit logging and role restriction. Security review required flag set on ticket.
2026-03-12 - Implementation: core router change committed (PR 1287). Integration tests green locally. Starting dry-run rollout flagged in Console for tenant: acme-marketing-1.
2026-03-12 - Follow-up: Marco assigned to finish dashboard widgets and add an alert in Console that surfaces sudden headroom drops for tenant operators.
